title: Bonds, Duration, Convexity, and Immunization

what: Duration and convexity of a cash-flow stream
title: Bonds, Duration, Convexity, and Immunization
text: payments C_j times t_j, P() = \sum_j C_j(1+)^{-t_j}. Define present-value weights w_j() = \frac{C_j(1+)^{-t_j}}{P()}. positive cash flows, Macaulay duration D_{\text{Mac}}() = \sum_j t_jw_j(), modified duration D_{\text{mod}}() = -\frac{1}{P()}\frac{dP()}{di} = \frac{D_{\text{Mac}}()}{1+}. Thus, \frac{\Delta P}{P} \approx -D_{\text{mod}}\Delta . Relative convexity C() = \frac{1}{P()}\frac{d^2P()}{di^2}, second-order approximation \frac{\Delta P}{P} \approx -D_{\text{mod}}\Delta + \frac12 C(\Delta )^2. Duration gives first-order approximation; convexity adds effect curvature.

title: Level annuity factor a-angle-n — a_angle
text: Supported timing conventions: "immediate": annuity-immediate discrete payments. "due": annuity-due discrete payments. "continuous": continuous annuity. discrete annuities, k number payments per year, payments made every \(1/k\) year. function returns annuity factor, assuming unit payment payment time. Deferment supported h. discrete annuities, deferment must align payment grid, , \(hk\) must integer. perpetuity = TRUE, infinite-term annuity factor returned. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: n: annuity term; k: payment frequency; : interest rate; i_type: interest-rate type; m: conversion frequency nominal rates; h: deferment period. function first converts supplied rate equivalent annual effective interest rate using standardize_interest. finite discrete annuities: $$a_{\overline{n|}} = \frac{1 - v^n}{}$$ due annuities: $$\ddot{}_{\overline{n|}} = (1+)a_{\overline{n|}}$$ continuous annuities: $$\bar{}_{\overline{n|}} = \frac{1 - e^{-\delta n}}{\delta}$$ Input vectors must length 1 common length. Missing values propagated.

title: Accumulation factor under conventional or time-varying interest — accumulation_factor
text: accumulation factor $$(s,t) = (1+)^{t-s}$$ constant annual effective rate, $$(s,t) = \frac{(t)}{(s)}$$ accumulation function, $$(s,t) = \exp\left(\int_s^t \delta(u)\,du\right)$$ time-varying force interest. Exactly one , , delta must supplied. Numeric arguments must length 1 common length. Scalars recycled remaining scenarios, making function suitable use inside dplyr::mutate() pipelines. Times must satisfy \(0 \le s \le t\). Missing times propagate missing accumulation factors.

title: Geometric annuity factor — annuity_geom
text: function covers finite geometric annuities geometric perpetuities. Supported timing conventions: "immediate": payments end period. "due": payments beginning period. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: n term, k payment frequency, interest-rate input, i_type interest-rate type, m conversion frequency nominal interest rates, g growth-rate input, g_type growth-rate type, g_m conversion frequency nominal growth rates, h deferment period, P1 first payment. Let \(i_p\) effective interest rate per payment period, \(g_p\) effective growth rate per payment period, \(v_p = (1+i_p)^{-1}\). finite geometric annuity-immediate \(N\) payment periods: $$ ga_N = \sum_{r=1}^{N}\frac{(1+g_p)^{r-1}}{(1+i_p)^r} $$ \(i_p \neq g_p\), $$ ga_N = \frac{1-\left(\frac{1+g_p}{1+i_p}\right)^N}{i_p-g_p}. $$ accumulated value factor computed standard terminal horizon: $$ gs_N = \sum_{r=1}^{N}(1+g_p)^{r-1}(1+i_p)^{N-r}. $$ annuities-due, corresponding immediate factor multiplied \(1+i_p\).

title: Actuarial present value of a multi-life annuity (up to 3 independent lives) — annuity_multi
text: implementation supports three lives, covers common practical multi-life arrangements. Supports status-based annuities (joint-life / last-survivor) joint--survivor style annuity ("reversionary") pays 1 lives alive pays fraction \(\alpha\) least one life remains alive. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: interest rate, i_type interest-rate type, m conversion frequency nominal rates, n term, h deferment period, k payment frequency. assumption independent future lifetimes, survival probability status calculated : Joint-life (first-death): \({}_t p_{x_1 x_2 \dots x_n} = \prod_{j=1}^n {}_t p_{x_j}\) Last-survivor: \({}_t p_{\overline{x_1 x_2 \dots x_n}} = 1 - \prod_{j=1}^n (1 - {}_t p_{x_j})\) annuity = "reversionary", APV weighted combination two statuses: $$APV = APV(\text{joint-life}) + \alpha [APV(\text{last-survivor}) - APV(\text{joint-life})].$$

text: function supports: whole-life annuities, temporary annuities, integer deferment, annual k-thly payments, exact fractional survival k-thly payments, first- second-order Woolhouse approximations. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: lt: life table; x: actuarial age; : interest rate; i_type: interest-rate type; m: interest conversion frequency; n: annuity term; h: deferment period; k: payment frequency. annual annuities-due, $$\ddot{}_{x:\overline{n}|} = \sum_{j=0}^{n-1} v^j\,{}_jp_x.$$ annual annuities-immediate, $$a_{x:\overline{n}|} = \sum_{j=1}^{n} v^j\,{}_jp_x.$$ Deferment handled $$v^h\,{}_hp_x,$$ \(h\) deferment period. k-thly payments woolhouse = "none", fractional survival computed selected fractional-age assumption. payment stream normalized annual payment rate 1: $$\ddot{}_{x:\overline{n}|}^{(k)} = \frac{1}{k}\sum_{j=0}^{kn-1} v^{j/k}\,{}_{j/k}p_x.$$ Consequently, k-thly installment amount \(1/k\). normalization essential function used premium annuity equivalence principle: resulting premium annualized, amount paid installment annualized premium divided \(k\).

text: function supports joint-life, last-survivor, state-based reversionary-style payments. life table input may either one common table lives list two life tables, one life. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: lt life table input, x y two actuarial ages, interest-rate input, i_type interest-rate type, m conversion frequency nominal rates, n term, h deferment period, k payment frequency. function assumes independent future lifetimes. state-based benefits, expected payment time \(t\) $$ b_{\text{}}\,{}_tp_x{}_tp_y + b_{x\text{ }}\,{}_tp_x(1-{}_tp_y) + b_{y\text{ }}\,{}_tp_y(1-{}_tp_x). $$ benefit = NULL, status = "joint" uses benefit = list(= 1, x_only = 0, y_only = 0), status = "last" uses benefit = list(= 1, x_only = 1, y_only = 1). k-thly payments, function values payment rate 1 per year, payment size \(1/k\). exact valuation, fractional term admissible whenever contains whole number payments: $$nk \\mathbb{N}.$$ Woolhouse approximations applied standard joint-life last-survivor statuses. deferred annuity, Woolhouse endpoint corrections multiplied issue-date value status beginning payment period. preserves deferment factor \(v^h\,{}_hp_{xy}\) last-survivor analogue.

title: Yield to maturity of a level coupon bond — bond_ytm
text: YTM solved first effective yield per coupon period reported together common annual equivalents. Assumptions: Coupons paid arrears regular intervals. Price observed coupon date (accrued interest). n * k must integer. Stub periods supported. function follows compact bond notation used tidyactuarial: P observed dirty price, face face value, c annual coupon rate, n time maturity, k coupon frequency, R redemption value. effective yield per coupon period \(j\) solution $$P = \sum_{r=1}^{N} C_r (1+j)^{-r}.$$ root found numerically using uniroot. interval supplied, function automatically brackets root starting \((-0.999999, 0.10)\) progressively widens upper bound sign change detected. per-period yield, annual equivalents : $$j^{(k)} = k j, \qquad = (1 + j)^k - 1.$$

title: Build an annual commutation table (discrete ages) — commutation_table
text: Constructs classical annual commutation functions \(D_x\), \(N_x\), \(S_x\), \(C_x\), \(M_x\), \(R_x\) life table defined integer ages, using compact actuarial notation. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: lt life table, interest-rate input, i_type interest-rate type, m conversion frequency nominal rates. annual effective rate obtained standardize_interest. \(i_e\) denotes annual effective rate, $$v = \frac{1}{1+i_e}.$$ annual deaths computed $$d_x = l_x - l_{x+1},$$ closing table \(l_{\omega+1}=0\). main commutation functions computed $$D_x = v^x l_x, \qquad C_x = v^{x+1} d_x,$$ reverse cumulative sums used obtain \(N_x\), \(S_x\), \(M_x\), \(R_x\).

title: Convexity of a general cash-flow stream — convexity_cash_flow
text: Let \(\tau\) valuation time. effective yield \(\), value remaining cash-flow stream $$ P_{\tau}() = \sum_{j:t_j>\tau} C_j(1+)^{-(t_j-\tau)}. $$ convexity returned function relative second derivative value respect effective yield: $$ \mathcal{C}_{\tau} = \frac{1}{P_{\tau}()} \frac{d^2P_{\tau}()}{di^2}. $$ Equivalently, $$ \mathcal{C}_{\tau} = \frac{ \sum_{j:t_j>\tau} (t_j-\tau)(t_j-\tau+1) C_j(1+)^{-(t_j-\tau+2)} }{ P_{\tau}() }. $$ Together modified duration, convexity gives second-order approximation $$ \frac{\Delta P_{\tau}}{P_{\tau}} \approx -D_{\mathrm{mod},\tau}\Delta + \frac{1}{2}\mathcal{C}_{\tau}(\Delta )^2. $$ function follows ex-cash-flow convention: cash flows occurring exactly valuation_time excluded. Therefore, result represents convexity immediately cash flow paid time. streams containing positive negative cash flows, convexity remains yield-sensitivity measure, may negative may usual interpretation associated conventional bonds.

title: Discount factor under conventional or time-varying interest — discount_factor
text: discount factor reciprocal corresponding accumulation factor: $$v(s,t) = \frac{1}{(s,t)}.$$ Therefore, $$v(s,t) = (1+)^{-(t-s)}$$ constant annual effective rate, $$v(s,t) = \frac{(s)}{(t)}$$ accumulation function, $$v(s,t) = \exp\left(-\int_s^t \delta(u)\,du\right)$$ time-varying force interest. title: Duration of a general cash-flow stream — duration_cash_flow
text: Let \(\tau\) valuation time. effective yield \(\), value remaining cash-flow stream $$ P_{\tau} = \sum_{j:t_j>\tau} C_j(1+)^{-(t_j-\tau)}. $$ Macaulay duration measured \(\tau\) $$ D_{\mathrm{Mac},\tau} = \frac{ \sum_{j:t_j>\tau} (t_j-\tau)C_j(1+)^{-(t_j-\tau)} }{ P_{\tau} }. $$ modified duration respect effective yield $$ D_{\mathrm{mod},\tau} = \frac{D_{\mathrm{Mac},\tau}}{1+}. $$ function follows ex-cash-flow convention: cash flows occurring exactly valuation_time excluded. Therefore, result represents duration immediately cash flow paid time. streams containing positive negative cash flows, duration remains yield-sensitivity measure, may usual interpretation weighted-average payment time.

title: Expected future lifetime from an annual life table — e_x
text: Curtate life expectancy (Finan, Section 23.7): $$e_x = \sum_{k=1}^{\omega - x} {}_k p_x = \frac{1}{\ell_x}   \sum_{k=1}^{\omega - x} \ell_{x+k}.$$ \(t\)-year temporary curtate expectancy (Finan, Sec. 23.7): $$e_{x:\overline{t}|} = \sum_{k=1}^{t} {}_k p_x.$$ Complete life expectancy (Finan, Section 23.3): $$\breve{e}_x = \int_0^{\omega - x} {}_t p_x \, dt =   \frac{T_x}{\ell_x}.$$ integral decomposed year--year. Within year, within-year survival integral \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du\) evaluated closed form selected fractional-age assumption (Finan, Section 24): UDD (Sec. 24.1): \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du = s - \frac{1}{2} s^2 q_y\) CF (Sec. 24.2): \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du = (1 - p_y^s) / (-\ln p_y)\) Balducci (Sec. 24.3): \(\int_0^s {}_u p_y \, du = \frac{p_y}{q_y} \ln \left( \frac{p_y + q_y s}{p_y} \right)\) UDD, complete expectancy satisfies well-known approximation (Finan, Example 20.24): $$\breve{e}_x \approx e_x + \frac{1}{2}.$$

title: Expected future lifetime for two independent lives — e_xy
text: Curtate expectation (Finan, Section 56.4 / Section 57): $$e_{xy} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} {}_kp_{xy}, \quad   e_{\overline{xy}} = \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} {}_kp_{\overline{xy}}.$$ Complete expectation (Finan, Section 56.4): $$\mathring{e}_{xy} = \int_0^{\infty} {}_tp_{xy} \, dt.$$ integral decomposed year--year. Within year, survival integral two-life status computed numerically via composite trapezoid (80-point grid), since closed-form expressions joint/last survivor fractional-age assumptions complex. Key identity (Finan, Example 57.4): $$\mathring{e}_{\overline{xy}} = \mathring{e}_x + \mathring{e}_y   - \mathring{e}_{xy}.$$ can used cross-validate results.

title: Expected future lifetime for two independent lives — e_xy
code: lt <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 99000, 97500, 95500, 93000, 90000, 86000) )  # Curtate joint-life expectancy (Finan, Sec. 56.4) e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, type = "curtate", cohort = "first") #> [1] NA  # Curtate last-survivor expectancy (Finan, Sec. 57) e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, type = "curtate", cohort = "last") #> [1] NA  # Verify identity (Finan, Example 57.4): # e_{xy-bar} = e_x + e_y - e_xy e_joint <- e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, type = "curtate", cohort = "first") e_last  <- e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, type = "curtate", cohort = "last") e_x_val <- e_x(lt, x = 60, type = "curtate") e_y_val <- e_x(lt, x = 62, type = "curtate") c(last_surv = e_last, sum_minus_joint = e_x_val + e_y_val - e_joint) #>       last_surv sum_minus_joint  #>              NA              NA   # Complete joint-life expectancy under UDD e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, type = "complete", frac = "UDD", cohort = "first") #> [1] NA  # Temporary: 3-year curtate joint-life e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 3, type = "curtate", cohort = "first") #> [1] 2.781231  # Tidy output e_xy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, type = "curtate", cohort = "first", tidy = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 7 #>       x     y     t type    frac  cohort    ex #>   <int> <int> <dbl> <chr>   <chr> <chr>  <dbl> #> 1    60    62    NA curtate UDD   first     NA

text: row treated one curve. tibble input, col_t col_i must list-columns equal-length numeric vectors, col_t_start col_t_end must numeric columns giving forward interval row. implied forward rate computed standardized annual effective spot curve : $$(1+i_1)^{t_1}(1+f)^{t_2-t_1}=(1+i_2)^{t_2}$$ $$f_{t_1,t_2} = \left(\frac{(1+i_2)^{t_2}}{(1+i_1)^{t_1}}\right)^{1/(t_2-t_1)} - 1.$$ Two extraction methods supported spot rates: "exact": requires t_start t_end match curve nodes. title: Duration-based immunization with multiple assets — immunize_duration
text: method enforces: present value assets = present value liabilities; Macaulay duration assets = Macaulay duration liabilities. exactly two assets, closed-form solution used. three assets, minimum-norm solution computed linear algebra. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: L denotes liabilities, t denotes payment times, P denotes asset prices present values, D denotes asset durations, denotes interest rate, i_type denotes interest-rate type, m denotes conversion frequency nominal rates. Let \(PV_L\) \(D_L\) present value Macaulay duration liability stream yield \(\). Let \(P_j\) \(D_j\) price duration asset \(j\). weights \(w_j\) chosen : $$\sum_j w_j P_j = PV_L$$ $$   \frac{\sum_j w_j P_j D_j}{\sum_j w_j P_j} = D_L. $$ two assets, closed-form solution : $$ w_1 = \frac{PV_L(D_L - D_2)}{P_1(D_1 - D_2)}, \qquad w_2 = \frac{PV_L - w_1 P_1}{P_2}. $$ three assets, minimum-norm solution linear system \(Aw = b\) computed, \(\) \(2 \times r\) matrix rows $$(P_1,\ldots,P_r)$$ $$(P_1D_1,\ldots,P_rD_r),$$ $$b = (PV_L, PV_LD_L)^T.$$

title: Kaplan–Meier survival curve and a lifetable-style life table — km_lifetable
text: resulting life table intended experience-based (empirical) life tables actuarial/demographic contexts (e.g., cohort studies, population indicators). replacement graduated/regulatory tables smoothing, extrapolation, product-specific selection effects required. Kaplan–Meier estimator. observed event time \(t_j\): $$\hat S(t) = \prod_{t_j \le t} \left(1 - \frac{d_j}{n_j}\right)$$ \(n_j\) risk set size \(d_j\) number events. Greenwood's variance: $$\widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(\hat S(t)) = \hat S(t)^2 \sum_{t_j \le t} \frac{d_j}{n_j(n_j - d_j)}.$$ Pointwise confidence intervals use log(-log) transformation. Life table mapping. interval \([x, x + \Delta)\): $$\ell_x = \text{radix} \cdot \hat S(x), \quad d_x = \ell_x -   \ell_{x+\Delta}, \quad q_x = d_x / \ell_x.$$ Exposure \(L_x = \int_x^{x+\Delta} \ell(t)\,dt\) computed using selected fractional-age assumption (Finan, Section 24): UDD (Finan, Sec. 24.1): \(L_x \approx \tfrac{\ell_x + \ell_{x+\Delta}}{2} \Delta\) CF (constant force, Finan, Sec. 24.2): \(L_x = \Delta \cdot (\ell_x - \ell_{x+\Delta}) /     \ln(\ell_x / \ell_{x+\Delta})\) Balducci (Finan, Sec. 24.3): \(L_x = \Delta \cdot \ell_x \ell_{x+\Delta} /     (\ell_x - \ell_{x+\Delta}) \cdot \ln(\ell_x / \ell_{x+\Delta})\) Additional columns follow Finan, Sections 23.3, 23.8–23.9: \(T_x = \sum_{k \ge x} L_k\): total expected years lived age \(x\) (Finan, Sec. 23.3). \(\mathring{e}_x = T_x / \ell_x\): complete life expectancy (Finan, Sec. 23.3). \(m_x = d_x / L_x\): central death rate (Finan, Sec. 23.9). \(a_x = (\ell_x \Delta - L_x) / d_x\): average fraction interval lived die.

title: Build an annual life table (tidy tibble) from lx, qx, px, or mx — lifetable
text: table can built exactly one : lx (survivors), qx (one-year death probabilities), px (one-year survival probabilities), mx (central death rates), function compute remaining columns consistently: dx, qx, px, mx. multiple inputs provided, priority : lx > qx > px > mx. lx provided together qx, cross-consistency validated (must agree via \(q_x = (\ell_x - \ell_{x+1}) / \ell_x\)). default, table actuarially closed omega: $$\ell_{\omega+1} = 0 \Rightarrow d_{\omega} = \ell_{\omega}       \Rightarrow q_{\omega} = 1 \Rightarrow p_{\omega} = 0.$$ life table follows standard actuarial construction described Finan, Sections 22–24 (Exam MLC preparation). basic identities (Finan, Section 22): $$\ell_x = \ell_0 \cdot s(x), \quad d_x = \ell_x - \ell_{x+1},       \quad q_x = d_x / \ell_x, \quad p_x = \ell_{x+1} / \ell_x.$$ central death rate mx computed via discrete approximation (Finan, Section 23.9): $$m_x = \frac{q_x}{1 - a_x \cdot q_x}$$ UDD (ax = 0.5) reduces classical formula \(m_x = q_x / (1 - 0.5 \, q_x)\) (Finan, Section 24.1). arises UDD, \(L_x = \ell_x - \tfrac{1}{2} d_x\), therefore \(m_x = d_x / L_x\). terminal age \(\omega\) close = TRUE, closure forces \(q_\omega = 1\), \(p_\omega = 0\), \(d_\omega = \ell_\omega\). corresponding \(m_\omega\) equals \(1/(1 - a_x)\), 2 UDD (ax = 0.5). ax = 1, \(m_\omega = \infty\).

title: Compute simulated present values for life insurance benefits — mc_insurance
text: function designed used simulate_lifetime, simulate_lifetimes, mc_multilife_status. takes simulated values curtate future lifetime \(K_x\), needed complete future lifetime \(T_x\), evaluates present value random variable associated classical life insurance benefits. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: interest-rate input, i_type interest-rate convention, m nominal conversion frequency, n insurance term, h deferral period. arguments m col_K deliberately different roles: m used nominal interest-rate conversion. col_K identifies simulated curtate future lifetime column. timing = "end_of_year", death benefits discounted using \(K_x + 1\). discrete convention, finite terms deferral periods must whole numbers years eligibility determined curtate lifetime \(K_x\). timing = "moment_of_death", death benefits discounted using \(T_x\), fractional terms deferral periods allowed. following insurance types supported: "whole": benefit paid whenever death occurs. "term": benefit paid death occurs within n years. "deferred": benefit paid death occurs deferral period h. "deferred_term": benefit paid death occurs h within following n years. "pure_endowment": benefit paid time n life survives time. "endowment": death benefit paid death occurs within n years; otherwise, survival benefit paid time n. function returns simulated present values, expected value. Therefore resulting column can summarized summary_mc, plotted ggplot2, used construct premiums, losses, reserves.

title: Compute Monte Carlo loss random variables for life contingencies — mc_loss
text: Let \(Z\) present value random variable benefits. Suppose col_Y contains $$ Y_c = c\sum_j v^{t_j}, $$ \(c\) amount used mc_annuity \(k\) premium dates per year. \(P^{(k)}\) annualized premium, actual installment \(P^{(k)}/k\), simulated present value premiums $$ \Pi = \frac{P^{(k)}}{k c}Y_c. $$ Hence loss issue $$ L = Z - \Pi. $$ recommended normalized premium annuity uses payment = 1 / k mc_annuity. \(c=1/k\), \(Y_c=Y^{(k)}\), expression simplifies $$ L = Z - P^{(k)}Y^{(k)}. $$ convention agrees premium_x, premium_xy, reserve_x, reserve_xy: premium annualized, amount collected date annualized premium divided k. backward compatibility, legacy columns P premium interpreted coefficients multiply supplied annuity present value directly. coefficient \(q\), $$ P_{\mathrm{per\ payment}} = q c, \qquad P^{(k)} = k q c. $$

title: Compute Monte Carlo prospective reserves for life contingencies — mc_reserve
text: Let \(Z_t\) present value duration \(t\) future benefits. Suppose future premium annuity constructed amount \(c\) \(k\) payment dates per year: $$ Y_{t,c}=c\sum_{j:t_j\ge t}v^{t_j-t}. $$ \(P^{(k)}\) annualized premium, installment \(P^{(k)}/k\) coefficient multiplying \(Y_{t,c}\) $$ q=\frac{P^{(k)}}{kc}. $$ Therefore simulated prospective loss $$ L_t=Z_t-qY_{t,c}. $$ recommended normalization payment = 1 / k, \(q=P^{(k)}\) $$ L_t=Z_t-P^{(k)}Y_t^{(k)}. $$ premium supplied, function estimates issue scale coefficient complete benefit-annuity simulation pairs: $$ \widehat q=\frac{\overline Z_0}{\overline Y_{0,c}}. $$ makes sample mean issue loss equal zero, numerical error, reserve_timing = "before_payment". column Y_t present value premium-annuity basis, including amount supplied payment. column future_pv_premiums actual simulated present value premium income, equal premium_annuity_scale * Y_t.

title: Generate a tidy life table from a theoretical mortality law — mortality_law_table
text: Exponential: \(\mu_x = \lambda\). Gompertz: \(\mu_x = Bc^x\). Makeham: \(\mu_x = + Bc^x\). Weibull: \(\mu_x = (shape/scale)(x/scale)^{shape-1}\). Logistic: \(\mu_x = (+ Bc^x)/(1 + Cc^x)\). title: Gross premium under a simple expense-loaded equivalence principle — premium_gross
text: function preserves package-wide distinction annualized premium amount paid k payment dates. Let \(^{(k)}\) denote APV premium annuity returned premium_x premium_xy. annuity \(k\) payments per year, amount \(1/k\); hence represents annual payment rate 1. \(P^{(k)}\) annualized net premium \(G^{(k)}\) annualized gross premium, extended equivalence equation implemented $$ G^{(k)}^{(k)} = P^{(k)}^{(k)} + \alpha\frac{G^{(k)}}{k} + \beta G^{(k)}^{(k)} + \gamma k ^{(k)}. $$ Therefore, $$ G^{(k)} = \frac{P^{(k)} + k\gamma} {(1-\beta)-\alpha/(k ^{(k)})}. $$ actual premium installment $$ G_{\mathrm{per\ payment}} = \frac{G^{(k)}}{k}. $$ k = 1, reduces previous annual formula: $$ G = \frac{P_{\mathrm{net}}+\gamma} {(1-\beta)-\alpha/}. $$ intentionally simple model assumes gamma incurred dates contingency premium payments. Expenses different timing contingency require APV represented gamma. Preferred column names prem premium_annualized, premium_per_payment, payments_per_year, apv_premium_annuity. Legacy annual tables using P, premium, P_net, a_premiums, apv_premiums remain supported. Legacy premium columns accepted automatically k = 1, unit ambiguous subannual premiums.

title: Sinking fund amortization schedule for a loan — sinking_fund_schedule
text: borrower pays: interest loan period, level deposit sinking fund. maturity, sinking fund used redeem principal. function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: loan interest rate, j sinking-fund accumulation rate, k number schedule periods per year, m conversion frequency loan rate, j_m conversion frequency sinking-fund rate. supplied annual rate specifications converted effective annual rates effective rates per schedule period: $$i_p = (1+i_e)^{1/k} - 1,\qquad       j_p = (1+j_e)^{1/k} - 1.$$ deposit NULL sinking-fund periodic rate j_p approximately zero, deposit computed principal / n. Otherwise, standard sinking-fund formula used: $$deposit = \frac{principal}{s_{\overline{n}|j_p}}$$ $$s_{\overline{n}|j_p} = \frac{(1+j_p)^n - 1}{j_p}.$$

title: Pure endowment (discounted survival): \({}_tE_x\) — t_Ex
text: Computes actuarial present value pure endowment, .e., expected present value payment 1 made time \(t\) life aged \(x\) survives age \(x + t\): $${}_tE_x = v^t \cdot {}_tp_x.$$

title: Pure endowment (discounted survival): \({}_tE_x\) — t_Ex
text: lt lifetable object produced lifetable. Must contain columns x lx. x Integer age(s) endowment starts. t Nonnegative numeric duration(s) years. Fractional durations allowed handled t_px. Annual interest-rate input(s). i_type Character vector indicating interest-rate type. Allowed values "effective", "nominal_interest", "nominal_discount", "force". m Positive integer vector giving conversion frequency nominal rates. Ignored "effective" "force". frac Fractional-age assumption passed t_px: "UDD", "CF", "CML" (alias CF), "Balducci". specified lt carries frac attribute, value used. tidy Logical. TRUE, returns tibble columns x, t, , i_type, m, i_effective, frac, nEx. check Logical. TRUE, performs validity checks. tol Numeric tolerance integer checks x.

title: Pure endowment (discounted survival): \({}_tE_x\) — t_Ex
text: Numeric vector \({}_tE_x\), tibble tidy = TRUE.

title: Pure endowment (discounted survival): \({}_tE_x\) — t_Ex
text: function follows compact actuarial notation used throughout tidyactuarial: lt life table, x age, t duration, interest-rate input, i_type interest-rate type, m conversion frequency nominal rates. pure endowment fundamental building block life contingency mathematics. serves actuarial discount factor, combining financial discounting mortality: $${}_tE_x = v^t \cdot {}_tp_x.$$ interest-rate input converted annual effective rate applying discount factor: $$v = (1+i_e)^{-1}.$$ Key identities involving \({}_nE_x\): Actuarial accumulated value: \(\ddot{s}_{x:\overline{n}|} = \ddot{}_{x:\overline{n}|} /     {}_nE_x\). Endowment insurance decomposition: \(A_{x:\overline{n}|} = ^1_{x:\overline{n}|} + {}_nE_x\). Deferred annuity: \({}_{n|}\ddot{}_x = {}_nE_x \cdot \ddot{}_{x+n}\). constant force mortality \(\mu\) force interest \(\delta\): $${}_nE_x = e^{-n(\mu + \delta)}.$$ variance pure endowment random variable : $$\mathrm{Var}(Z) = v^{2n} \cdot {}_np_x \cdot {}_nq_x.$$

title: Pure endowment (discounted survival): \({}_tE_x\) — t_Ex
code: x  <- 0:5 lx <- c(100000, 99500, 99000, 98200, 97000, 95000) lt <- lifetable(x = x, lx = lx, omega = 5, close = TRUE)  # Basic pure endowment: 3_E_0 = v^3 * 3_p_0 t_Ex(lt, x = 0, t = 3, i = 0.06) #> [1] 0.8245061  # Verify manually: (1.06)^(-3) * t_px(lt, x = 0, t = 3) #> [1] 0.8245061  # Constant force of interest lt_exp <- lifetable(x = 0:50, lx = 100000 * exp(-0.05 * (0:50))) t_Ex(   lt_exp,   x = 30,   t = 10,   i = 0.10,   i_type = "force" ) #> [1] 0.2231302 exp(-1.5) #> [1] 0.2231302  # Nominal annual interest rate convertible monthly t_Ex(   lt,   x = 0,   t = 3,   i = 0.06,   i_type = "nominal_interest",   m = 12 ) #> [1] 0.8206033  # Vectorized: multiple ages at once t_Ex(lt, x = c(0, 1, 2), t = 3, i = 0.05, tidy = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 3 × 8 #>       x     t     i i_type        m i_effective frac    nEx #>   <int> <dbl> <dbl> <chr>     <int>       <dbl> <chr> <dbl> #> 1     0     3  0.05 effective     1        0.05 UDD   0.848 #> 2     1     3  0.05 effective     1        0.05 UDD   0.842 #> 3     2     3  0.05 effective     1        0.05 UDD   0.829  # Use in a tidy pipeline if (requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) {   tibble::tibble(x = 0:4, t = c(5, 4, 3, 2, 1)) |>     dplyr::mutate(pure_endow = t_Ex(lt, x = x, t = t, i = 0.06)) } #> # A tibble: 5 × 3 #>       x     t pure_endow #>   <int> <dbl>      <dbl> #> 1     0     5      0.710 #> 2     1     4      0.756 #> 3     2     3      0.806 #> 4     3     2      0.861 #> 5     4     1      0.924

what: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
title: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
text: Computes t-year survival probability $${}_t p_x = P[T(x) > t]$$ using annual life table, allowing fractional ages standard actuarial assumptions.

title: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
code: t_px(lt, x, t, frac, tidy = FALSE, check = TRUE, tol = 1e-10)

title: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
text: lt lifetable object produced lifetable. Must contain columns x lx. Columns qx px used present. x Integer age(s) survival starts. t Nonnegative numeric duration(s) years (can fractional). frac Fractional-age assumption: "UDD", "CF", "CML" (alias CF), "Balducci". specified lt carries frac attribute (set lifetable), value used. tidy Logical. TRUE, returns tibble columns x, t, frac, tpx. check Logical. TRUE, performs validity checks. tol Numeric tolerance integer checks x.

title: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
text: Numeric vector \({}_t p_x\), tibble tidy = TRUE.

title: t-year survival probability from a life table — t_px
text: integer-year survival obtained directly life table (Finan, Section 22): $${}_n p_x = \frac{\ell_{x+n}}{\ell_x}$$ non-integer durations, let \(t = n + s\) \(n = \lfloor t \rfloor\) \(s \[0,1)\). (Finan, Section 24): $${}_t p_x = {}_n p_x \times {}_s p_{x+n}$$ fractional-year factor \({}_s p_y\) depends assumption: UDD (Finan, Sec. 24.1): \({}_s p_y = 1 - s \times q_y\) CF (Finan, Sec. 24.2): \({}_s p_y = (p_y)^s\) Balducci (Finan, Sec. 24.3): \({}_s p_y = \frac{p_y}{1 - (1 - s) \times q_y}\) \(x + t > \omega\) (terminal age), function returns 0 since survival possible beyond table's limiting age.

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy
text: lt Either: single life table data frame, used lives; list two life tables list(lt_x, lt_y), one life. life table must contain columns x lx. x Integer actuarial age first life time 0. y Integer actuarial age second life time 0. t Nonnegative time (may fractional). frac Fractional-age assumption: "UDD", "CF", "CML" (alias CF), "Balducci". specified supplied life table(s) carry frac attribute, value used. two tables supplied frac attributes differ, frac must supplied explicitly. Passed t_px. status Two-life status: "joint" "last".

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy
text: single numeric value.

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy
text: Independence assumed throughout (Finan, Sections 56–57). Joint-life status (Finan, Section 56): status survives long lives alive. $${}_tp_{xy} = {}_tp_x \cdot {}_tp_y.$$ Last-survivor status (Finan, Section 57): status survives long least one life alive. $${}_tp_{\overline{xy}} = {}_tp_x + {}_tp_y - {}_tp_x \cdot {}_tp_y.$$ Individual survival probabilities \({}_tp_x\) \({}_tp_y\) computed via t_px, supports fractional ages UDD, constant force, Balducci assumptions (Finan, Section 24).

title: Two-life survival probability for independent lives — t_pxy
code: lt <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 99000, 97500, 95500, 93000, 90000, 86000) )  # Joint life, 2.5 years, UDD (Finan, Sec. 56) t_pxy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD", status = "joint") #> [1] 0.9056154  # Verify: joint = product of marginals t_px(lt, x = 60, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD") *   t_px(lt, x = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD") #> [1] 0.9056154  # Last survivor, 2.5 years, constant force (Finan, Sec. 57) t_pxy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "CF", status = "last") #> [1] 0.9978385  # Same result if the same table is supplied explicitly for both lives t_pxy(list(lt, lt), x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD", status = "joint") #> [1] 0.9056154  # Different life tables for the two lives lt_m <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 98500, 96800, 94800, 92400, 89500, 86000) ) lt_f <- data.frame(   x  = 60:66,   lx = c(100000, 99000, 97800, 96400, 94700, 92700, 90300) ) t_pxy(list(lt_m, lt_f), x = 60, y = 62, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD", status = "joint") #> [1] 0.9178384  # Finan Example 56.2 style: integer survival # 10_p_{50:60} = 10_p_50 * 10_p_60 lt_ilt <- data.frame(   x  = 50:70,   lx = c(8950901, 8879913, 8804189, 8723382, 8637048,          8544731, 8445974, 8340310, 8227261, 8106334,          7977338, 7839775, 7693040, 7536522, 7369603,          7191658, 7002051, 6800139, 6585264, 6356752,          6114913) ) t_pxy(lt_ilt, x = 50, y = 60, t = 10, status = "joint") #> [1] NA  # Finan Problem 56.1: t_q_xy = t_q_x + t_q_y - t_q_x * t_q_y p_joint <- t_pxy(lt, x = 60, y = 62, t = 3, status = "joint") q_joint <- 1 - p_joint qx <- 1 - t_px(lt, x = 60, t = 3) qy <- 1 - t_px(lt, x = 62, t = 3) c(q_joint = q_joint, q_sum = qx + qy - qx * qy)  # should match #>   q_joint     q_sum  #> 0.1184615 0.1184615

code: t_qx(lt, x, t, frac, tidy = FALSE, check = TRUE, tol = 1e-10)

title: t-year death probability from a life table — t_qx
text: lt lifetable object produced lifetable. Must contain columns x lx. Columns qx px used present. x Integer age(s) interval starts. t Nonnegative numeric duration(s) years (can fractional). frac Fractional-age assumption: "UDD", "CF", "CML" (alias CF), "Balducci". specified lt carries frac attribute (set lifetable), value used. Passed directly t_px. tidy Logical. TRUE, returns tibble columns x, t, frac, tqx. check Logical. TRUE, performs validity checks. tol Numeric tolerance integer checks x.

title: t-year death probability from a life table — t_qx
text: Numeric vector \({}_t q_x\), tibble tidy = TRUE.

title: t-year death probability from a life table — t_qx
text: thin wrapper around t_px: $${}_t q_x = 1 - {}_t p_x.$$ identity \({}_tq_x = {}_td_x / \ell_x\) (Finan, Section 22) holds integer \(t\), \({}_td_x = \ell_x - \ell_{x+t}\) expected number deaths ages \(x\) \(x+t\). fractional durations, result depends chosen assumption (UDD, CF, Balducci); see t_px details formulas (Finan, Section 24). deferred death probability \({}_{n|}q_x\) can obtained (Finan, Section 23.4): $${}_{n|}q_x = {}_np_x \cdot q_{x+n} = {}_{n+1}q_x - {}_nq_x.$$

title: t-year death probability from a life table — t_qx
code: x  <- 0:5 lx <- c(100000, 99500, 99000, 98200, 97000, 95000) lt <- lifetable(x = x, lx = lx, omega = 5, close = TRUE)  # Integer death probability (Finan, Section 22) t_qx(lt, x = 0, t = 3)  # (l0 - l3) / l0 #> [1] 0.018  # t = 0 always returns 0 t_qx(lt, x = 0, t = 0) #> [1] 0  # Fractional age under UDD (Finan, Section 24.1) t_qx(lt, x = 0, t = 2.5, frac = "UDD") #> [1] 0.014  # Finan Example 22.2a: number of deaths between ages 2 and 5 # 3_d_2 = l_2 - l_5 = 98995 - 97468 = 1527 lt_22 <- lifetable(   x = 0:5,   lx = c(100000, 99499, 98995, 98489, 97980, 97468) ) t_qx(lt_22, x = 2, t = 3) * lt_22$lx[lt_22$x == 2]  # 1527 #> [1] 1527  # Deferred death probability (Finan, Section 23.4): # 2|1_q_0 = 2_p_0 * q_2 = 3_q_0 - 2_q_0 t_qx(lt, x = 0, t = 3) - t_qx(lt, x = 0, t = 2) #> [1] 0.008  # Vectorized with tidy output t_qx(lt, x = c(0, 1), t = c(1.5, 2.2), frac = "Balducci", tidy = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 2 × 4 #>       x     t frac         tqx #>   <int> <dbl> <chr>      <dbl> #> 1     0   1.5 Balducci 0.00751 #> 2     1   2.2 Balducci 0.0155   # Use in a tidy pipeline if (requireNamespace("dplyr", quietly = TRUE)) {   tibble::tibble(age = c(0, 1, 2), duration = c(3, 2.5, 1.7)) |>     dplyr::mutate(       surv  = t_px(lt, x = age, t = duration),       death = t_qx(lt, x = age, t = duration)     ) } #> # A tibble: 3 × 4 #>     age duration  surv  death #>   <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl> #> 1     0      3   0.982 0.0180 #> 2     1      2.5 0.981 0.0191 #> 3     2      1.7 0.983 0.0166

title: t-year probability of decrement by cause j: t_qxj — t_qxj

title: t-year probability of decrement by cause j: t_qxj — t_qxj
text: md multiple decrement table produced md_table. Must contain columns x, p_total, requested cause. x Numeric vector. Starting age(s) (integer-valued). t Numeric vector. Time horizon(s) years (t >= 0). Can non-integer frac supplied. cause Character. Name cause column md (e.g., "q_death"). frac Character. Fractional-age assumption non-integer t: one "UDD", "CF", "Balducci", NULL. NULL (default), t must integer-valued. tidy Logical. TRUE, returns tibble columns x, t, cause, frac, tqxj. check Logical. TRUE, performs input validation (default TRUE). tol Numeric tolerance integer checks (default 1e-10).

title: t-year probability of decrement by cause j: t_qxj — t_qxj
text: Numeric vector \({}_t q_x^{(j)}\) (tibble tidy=TRUE).

title: t-year probability of decrement by cause j: t_qxj — t_qxj
text: Let \(q_x^{(j)}\) annual decrement probability cause \(j\) \(q_x^{(\tau)}\) total decrement probability. integer \(t\), $$ {}_t q_x^{(j)} = \sum_{k=0}^{t-1} \left(\prod_{r=0}^{k-1} p_{x+r}^{(\tau)}\right) q_{x+k}^{(j)}. $$ non-integer \(t = n + s\) \(n = \lfloor t \rfloor\) \(s \[0,1)\), function supports fractional-age assumptions specified frac uses additional convention within-year cause proportions remain constant: \({}_s q_x^{(j)} = w_j \, {}_s q_x^{(\tau)}\) \(w_j = q_x^{(j)} / q_x^{(\tau)}\) (0 \(q_x^{(\tau)}=0\)). Supported fractional-age assumptions total decrement: "UDD": \({}_s q_x^{(\tau)} = s q_x^{(\tau)}\). "CF":  \({}_s p_x^{(\tau)} = (p_x^{(\tau)})^s\). "Balducci": \({}_s q_x^{(\tau)} = \frac{s q_x^{(\tau)}}{1-(1-s)q_x^{(\tau)}}\).

title: t-year probability of decrement by cause j: t_qxj — t_qxj
code: qx_df <- tibble::tibble(   x = 30:35,   q_death = c(0.001, 0.0012, 0.0014, 0.0017, 0.0020, 1.0000),   q_disability = c(0.002, 0.0021, 0.0022, 0.0023, 0.0024, 0.0000) ) md <- md_table(qx_df, radix = 1e5, close = TRUE) t_qxj(md, x = 30, t = 5, cause = "q_death") #> [1] 0.007243163 t_qxj(md, x = 30, t = 2.5, cause = "q_death", frac = "CF", tidy = TRUE) #> # A tibble: 1 × 5 #>       x     t cause   frac     tqxj #>   <int> <dbl> <chr>   <chr>   <dbl> #> 1    30   2.5 q_death CF    0.00289
